# `tfctl auth login`

The `tfctl auth login` command authenticates with HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ tfctl auth login [options]
```

## Description

The `tfctl auth login` command authenticates tfctl with HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise. The CLI stores your token in your active profile configuration, and uses it for all API calls that require authentication.

When `--token` is specified, tfctl reads the token from standard input. Use this option for non-interactive environments such as CI/CD pipelines.

When `--token` is not specified, tfctl opens a browser to the token creation page for the configured hostname. Refer to [Example: Set a custom hostname](/terraform/tfctl-cli/authenticate#set-hostname) to learn how to set your hostname. The page prompts the user to copy and paste the generated token.

## Available options

The `tfctl auth login` command supports the following options.

| Option | Description | Default | Required |
|--------|-------------|---------|----------|
| `--token` | Read the token from standard input instead of prompting. When this flag is used, tfctl reads the token from stdin without opening a browser. | `false` | No |

### Global flags

Refer to [Global flags reference](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli#global-flags) for information about flags you can use with all commands.

## Examples

The following examples demonstrate how to authenticate with HCP Terraform using the `tfctl auth login` command.

### Interactive login

The following example opens your browser to create a token, then prompts you to paste it.

```shell-session
$ tfctl auth login
```

### Login with token from stdin

The following example reads the token from stdin without opening a browser or prompting for input. This is useful for CI/CD pipelines and other non-interactive environments. Replace `<MY_TOKEN>` with your HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise API token.

```shell-session
$ echo <MY_TOKEN> | tfctl auth login --token
```
